title: ComplianceReport
description: The evidence-backed verdict for one generated song. Returned to the user alongside the artifact. States per requirement what was checked, by whom, with what evidence, and what the verdict was. A requirement that was not checked is 'unverified', never 'met'.

oracle.description: Which oracle answered, and which version, so a verdict can be re-derived later.

degraded_reason.description: Set when the oracle failed and semantic checks fell back to unverified.

overall.description: compliant requires every hard and policy requirement met and no requirement uncertain.

unmet.description: The explicit list of what the system could not satisfy. This is the honest-output contract: it is never empty when overall is not 'compliant'.

counts.description: The two headline counts. 'Twelve met, six of them on description' is a different document from 'twelve met', and only one of them is honest.

decided_by_measurement.description: Met verdicts resting on arithmetic or signal processing. The number to trust.

decided_by_description.description: Met verdicts resting on a model's generated account. The number to watch, because it can be inflated without anyone noticing.

cross_check.description: The 'is any requirement seriously violated' summary question, reported alongside the individual verdicts and never as a substitute for them.

iterations.description: How many repair rounds ran before this candidate was returned.

checker.description: The verify field from the spec, echoed so the report shows who decided.

verdict.description: uncertain = inside the uncertainty band. unverified = not checked, e.g. the oracle was unreachable. Neither is a pass.

probability.description: The oracle's noul, or the top-option probability, for semantic requirements.

confidence.description: Recorded for completeness and audit, not used for gating; the top-two margin is the discrimination signal.

enforcement.description: How strongly this requirement could be checked, given the chosen generator. Read from the requirement taxonomy; absent when that mapping has not been made.

evidence_class.description: What kind of evidence the verdict rests on. A hard requirement may not be met on description alone, and a self-report never decides one, so the gate caps such a verdict at 'uncertain' rather than at 'met'.

supported_by.description: The evidence behind the verdict, each item carrying its own class and source, so a wrong verdict can be traced to the model or measurement that produced it.

source.description: Which model or checker, carrying its version or revision, because 'the captioner said so' is not reproducible.

value.description: The reading itself: a probability, a level with its top probability, or a measured number.

threshold.description: The threshold that decided. Recorded because thresholds do not port between questions, primitives or model versions.

note.description: Why this verdict and not another, in a sentence: the band it fell in, the gate it missed, or what the evidence was.

measured.description: For code and audio checkers: the actual measured value and the target it was compared against.

evidence.description: Pointers to the exact material the checker read, so a wrong verdict can be traced to a wrong input.
